text: Systems thinking, traceable requirements, evidence and illustrative design-option scoring
Learn to define a system, write clear requirements, select evidence, and compare fictional design options. Eight untimed activities support practice.
Designed for first-time learners, without specialized engineering prerequisites.

You need only this HTML file and a browser. A live multi-team auction is not included. No network account is required. File release 1.0.0-rc.2 uses study runtime 1.5.5. For upgrades, export progress from the previous file before restoring it in this version.
Identify boundaries and interfaces, choose evidence, compute fictional capability totals, test mandatory conditions, compare prices and explain model limitations.
Begin with seven Essentials chapters. Read the Core chapters and proposed multiplayer lessons when their topics matter.
Read a chapter and answer its checks. Practice one related activity, then save progress from My Progress before changing devices.

items: Describe the intended result before choosing parts.
Identify essential interfaces and outside constraints.
State important requirements so someone can test them.
Meet every compulsory threshold before awarding optional points.
Keep positive and negative effects when totaling fictional cards.
Base costs on actual accepted purchase prices, not starting offers.
Distinguish reported workshop rules from the later proposed connected-product design.

text: A design cannot earn eligibility by accumulating bonus points while missing a required condition.

Start with the intended outcome, operating conditions and people affected. Map system boundaries and dependencies before writing testable requirements. Compare technical choices alongside evidence, support, risk and future operating costs. In the classroom model, added card effects change numbers; meet every required threshold before scoring optional value. The online auction material describes a proposed product, not a working shared service.

items: Need and operating context → system boundary and links
Fictional option cards → signed attribute totals
Required thresholds → optional points → offer comparison
Local practice → separate proposed real-time implementation
